summary: The route table. It maps each hash path (`#/events`, `#/lab`, ...) to its page module and defines the two-key g-then-letter shortcuts; `main.js` looks pages up in `PAGES` inside `route()` and reads `SHORTCUTS` in its keyboard handler. Adding a page means writing a module that exports `{ title, render }` and registering it here (plus, to make it reachable, a nav link in `index.html` and an entry in the palette).

notes.text: Header comment describing the **page contract**: every page module default-exports an object with a `title` and a `render(view, ctx, params)` function (usually `async`), which `route()` calls with the outlet element, the cleanup context and the URL query parameters.
Default-imports each page module, i.e. the `{ title, render }` object it exports. The list is alphabetical: AI Analyst, Events, Incidents and Integration here.

The remaining pages: Risk Lab, Overview, Simulation and Customers (`users.js`). These are static imports, so all eight pages load up front together with `main.js` and switching pages never waits for code to download.

`PAGES` maps hash paths to page modules using object shorthand (`overview` means `overview: overview`), so `#/lab` renders `PAGES.lab`. `route()` falls back to `overview` for any path that is not a key here.
Comment: shortcuts are two-key sequences, 'g' followed by a letter.

`SHORTCUTS` maps the second key to a page: usually its first letter, except `c` for Customers (whose route is `users`) and `n` for Integration, because `i` already means Incidents. The keyboard handler in `main.js` reads it, and the nav hints and the palette show the same letters.
